label: Crush and pinch points
summary: Things that fall, tip, close or move: vehicles slipping off jacks, tall machines tipping over, motorised beds and lifts moving when you don't expect it, and fingers caught in gears, chains, belts and scissor linkages.
signs: Anything held up by a jack, hydraulics, a spring or a single prop
Tall heavy items: vending machines, shelving racks, fridges, safes and cabinets
Scissor linkages in lifts, recliners and hospital beds
Machines with batteries that could still move: stairlifts, power chairs, lifts, garage doors
Doors and gates with closers or motors
do: Support anything raised with stands or solid timber blocks, never a jack alone
Jack only on firm, level ground, and chock the wheels that stay on the ground every time
Disconnect batteries and power so mechanisms can't move
Keep hands out of the path of anything that could move or close
Plan where a heavy item will fall and keep a clear escape route
Work with a second person who can get help
dont: Don't get under a vehicle or load held only by a jack
Don't rock or tip vending machines or tall shelving
Don't reach into linkages, gears or belts to clear a jam while there is power
Don't wear loose sleeves, gloves or long loose hair near spinning parts: for shafts, augers, drills and belts that wind clothes or hair in, see Entanglement in rotating machinery
Don't prop a vehicle or load on bricks, hollow concrete blocks or stacked junk: they can crumble without warning
firstAid: Free a trapped person as quickly as you safely can, then get medical help: long crush injuries can harm the kidneys hours later
Crushed finger: cool it and raise it; a bent or badly swollen finger may be broken
A crushed chest with difficult breathing is an emergency

After a long trapping, give plenty to drink in the first hours if they are awake and can swallow, and watch for dark, cola-coloured or very little urine: that means kidney trouble and needs medical care

sources.title: OSHA 3170: OSHA 3170, Safeguarding Equipment and Protecting Employees from Amputations
